title: OpenAI'ın GPT-6 Astra modeli hukuk ve video düzenlemede kullanılmaya başladı
summary: OpenAI, yeni nesil modeli GPT-6 Astra'nın Harvey, invideo ve Airbnb gibi platformlar tarafından kullanılmaya başlandığını duyurdu.
body:
OpenAI'ın duyurusuna göre, yeni nesil dil modeli **GPT-6 Astra** iş dünyasında ve farklı sektörlerde kullanılmaya başlandı. Hukuk teknolojileri şirketi Harvey, video düzenleme platformu invideo ve konaklama devi Airbnb, operasyonlarında bu yeni modeli entegre eden kurumlar arasında yer alıyor.

## Hukuk ve video düzenlemede Astra etkisi

OpenAI'ın aktardığına göre, **Harvey** adlı yapay zeka destekli hukuk platformu, GPT-6 Astra sayesinde karmaşık hukuki bağlamları daha iyi işleyebiliyor. Model, mahkeme bilgileri ve dava araştırmaları gibi geniş veri kaynaklarını daha yapılı çıktılara dönüştürürken, platforma eklenen hafıza paneli avukatların tercihlerini doğrudan taslak süreçlerine yansıtmasına imkan tanıyor. Diğer yandan, yapay zeka odaklı video editörü invideo da Astra ile renk düzenleme ve düzeltme görevlerinde başarısını üç kat artırdı. Şirket, modelin yardımıyla tek bir günde 50 özel efekt üretebildiğini bildirdi.

## Airbnb mühendisliğinde genişleyen kullanım

Airbnb ise yaptığı yeni bir anlaşmayla mühendislik ve ürün geliştirme ekiplerinin GPT-6 Astra dahil olmak üzere OpenAI öncü modellerine erişimini genişletti. Amazon Bedrock ve OpenAI API'leri üzerinden sağlanan bu erişim, Airbnb mühendislerinin kod yazma, hata ayıklama ve sistem tasarımı süreçlerini hızlandırmasına yardımcı oluyor. Şirket ayrıca yapay zeka modellerini arama, dolandırıcılık önleme, müşteri desteği ve sigorta talepleri gibi alanlarda da kullanıyor.

**Neden önemli?** GPT-6 Astra'nın kurumsal entegrasyonları, büyük dil modellerinin hukuk, video prodüksiyonu ve yazılım mühendisliği gibi karmaşık iş akışlarında daha fazla bağlam işleme ve daha az işlem adımıyla yüksek doğruluk sağlama kapasitesini gösteriyor.

source_texts.title: Harvey turns legal context into stronger drafts with GPT-6 Astra
source_texts.summary: GPT-6 Astra produces more structured, context-aware legal documents, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy.
source_texts.text:
Harvey helps law firms and in-house legal teams securely deploy AI across complex legal workflows, from litigation to mergers. Its customers use Harvey to turn vast amounts of information into complex legal documents. With GPT‑6 Astra, Harvey can bring more context into the drafting process and generate more structured outputs.
“We can give more context to the model and produce better and better structured outputs.”
Harvey uses GPT‑6 Astra to help lawyers analyze, synthesize, and draft from the information that shapes a matter, including court information, law firm documents, case law research, and other sources of legal context.
Compared with other models, Harvey has seen substantial improvements in document formatting and context awareness with GPT‑6 Astra, helping customers get more complete documents that better reflect the material behind them.
Harvey’s memory panel brings individual preferences directly into the drafting workflow. A lawyer can encode preferences such as using numbered lists, prioritizing EDGAR as a source, or color coding issues by priority.
Those preferences appear alongside the source material and the draft memorandum, giving the lawyer a clearer way to guide the output. Because GPT‑6 Astra can process more context, Harvey can produce higher-quality legal documents while customers focus more of their time on strategy.

source_texts.title: How invideo improves color grading 3x with GPT‑6 Astra
source_texts.summary: With GPT‑6 Astra, invideo plans edits with greater precision, improves color correction and grading threefold, and produces 50 custom effects in one day.
source_texts.text:
How invideo improves color grading 3x with GPT‑6 Astra
With GPT‑6 Astra, invideo plans edits with greater precision, improves color correction and grading threefold, and produces 50 custom effects in one day.
Results
50
Custom effects created in one day
Results
3x
Increase in success rate for color-grading and correction
Editing videos is one creative and technical decision after another. Editors have to shape the story, place sound effects, build transitions, adjust color, and more. Invideo(opens in a new window) is an agentic video editor designed to handle that work while keeping the human editor in control.
With GPT‑6 Astra, invideo sees greater capability to plan and execute complex edits and place changes at the correct points in the timeline.
“How Astra can plan a particular edit on a frame-level accuracy is quite stunning.”
The AI agent must translate the editor’s direction into a sequence of steps, choose the right tools, execute the work, and verify the result. Sanket says GPT‑6 Astra can plan these operations in fewer reasoning steps than the models it previously tested: “Astra is using far fewer reasoning sets and thus output tokens to complete complex work.”
Invideo also observed that Astra can carry out several instructions without losing the editor’s original objective as the task grows longer and more complex.
GPT‑6 Astra is especially effective when it comes to color work, where the agent must choose from overlapping approaches such as correction, grading, regeneration, LUTs, and isolation. For example, changing a background while preserving a person’s skin tone requires the agent to isolate and track the person across frames before applying color elsewhere.
“Earlier, we saw very high failure rates for color-grading and color-correction tasks. With Astra, the success rate improved about three times,” said Sanket.
GPT‑6 Astra also helps invideo turn descriptions and visual references into custom effects. The agent can code an effect tailored to the footage, place it on the timeline, and add controls that let the editor refine it. In one day, a few Invideo editors used the model to create about 50 effects.
With the invideo agent using GPT‑6 Astra, creative professionals retain control of the story, their taste, and the final cut without losing hours to the tedious planning and frame-by-frame work.

source_texts.title: Airbnb widens access to GPT-6 Astra and OpenAI frontier models
source_texts.summary: Learn how Airbnb is expanding access to GPT-6 Astra and OpenAI frontier models to help engineering teams solve bugs, design systems, and ship faster.
source_texts.text:
Under a new agreement, Airbnb is giving its engineering and product development teams broader access to OpenAI frontier models, including GPT‑6 Astra.
The expansion builds on Airbnb’s use of Codex and longstanding collaboration with OpenAI. Airbnb engineers use an internal AI assistant for writing software and creating remote AI agents powered by Codex and models like GPT‑5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna.
The new agreement gives Airbnb broader access to OpenAI models through OpenAI APIs and Amazon Bedrock. It arrives amid accelerating adoption of GPT‑6 Astra among developers, builders, and enterprises, many of which were already benefiting from the improved price-performance and efficiency of GPT‑5.6 Terra and Luna.
Airbnb’s early use of GPT‑6 Astra has shown strong results beyond coding. Astra helps Airbnb engineers accelerate their work by tracking down hard bugs, shaping system designs, and brainstorming engineering approaches. In one test involving strategic documents and other non-coding work, one Airbnb user reported reaching impressive output in 3–4 passes, compared with 20+ rounds using other models.
Airbnb also uses OpenAI models to help support experiences across search, fraud prevention, guest and host support, and insurance claims. This deep use of AI and machine learning across its marketplace helps the company better understand what guests are looking for, identify potentially fraudulent content or claims, help guests when travel plans change, and ensure hosts get insurance payouts faster and easier.
As Airbnb brings more of the trip into one app—across homes, services, experiences, airport pickups, car rentals, and more—OpenAI frontier models can give the teams building those features more powerful tools to move faster and explore what comes next.
